newsitem.title: USA: Fight brews for Massport top job - reports.
newsitem.headline: Fight brews for Massport top job - reports.

text.p: Defeated Republican congressman Peter Blute, tipped by Massachusetts Governor William Weld to become the new executive director of the Massachusetts Port Authority, has run into some opposition -- from Weld's own appointees to the board, according to published reports.

Several board members, all Weld appointees, said despite pressure from the governor they will not automatically approve the Shrewsbury Republican's appointment to succeed Stephen Tocco, who formally submitted his resignation Thursday, The Boston Globe reported.
The Boston Herald said the six board members present at the regular meeting voted to set up a committee to review candidates for the job, which pays $104,000 annually.
In a related action, the board approved a contract for Tocco of up to six months at his present salary level after he leaves on Dec. 1, so he can help with the transition.
Weld has already asked Blute to take the job, but Blute has not announced his decision.
